eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Ten
subtitle: Lesson 84 · Window and Ranking Functions

eyebrow: The first row of the window
code:
SELECT Name, Color, ListPrice,
  FIRST_VALUE(Name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC)
    AS MostExpensiveInColor
FROM Production.Product;
caption: The most expensive product name, attached to every row in its color.

code:
SELECT Name, Color, ListPrice,
  LAST_VALUE(Name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC)
    AS SupposedlyCheapest
FROM Production.Product;
-- Returns the CURRENT ROW's own name, not the cheapest
caption: Not a bug — the default frame is doing exactly what it's defined to do.

code:
-- Default frame with ORDER BY and no explicit frame:
-- RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
-- "Last" visible row = the current row, every time
caption: LAST_VALUE can only see up to the current row by default.

code:
LAST_VALUE(Name) OVER (
  PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC
  ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
    AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
) AS CheapestInColor
caption: Now the frame is the WHOLE partition — before and after the current row.
